mil3.2.6:1.4: “Name and form is reborn, Great King.”
mil3.2.6:1.5: “Is it just this very name and form that is reborn?”
mil3.2.6:1.6: “It is not just this very name and form that is reborn, Great King. Rather, Great King, with this name and form one does a deed, good or bad, and by that deed another name and form is reborn.”
mil3.2.6:1.7: “If, venerable sir, it is not just this very name and form that is reborn, will he not be free from bad deeds?”
mil3.2.6:1.9: “If he were not reborn, he would be free from bad deeds.
mil3.2.6:1.10: But because he is reborn, Great King, he is not free from bad deeds.”
mil3.2.6:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to steal a mango from another man, and the owner of the mango, having seized him, were to show him to the king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, this man stole my mangoes’. He would say: ‘Your Majesty, I did not steal this man’s mangoes. The mangoes that he planted were different mangoes; the mangoes that I stole were different mangoes. I am not liable to punishment’.
mil3.2.6:2.3: Would that man be liable to punishment, Great King?”
mil3.2.6:2.6: “Even if he said so, venerable sir, since he cannot disown the earlier mango, that man would be liable to punishment because of the later mango.”
mil3.2.6:2.7: “In the same way, Great King, with this name and form one does a deed, good or bad, and by that deed another name and form is reborn; therefore he is not free from bad deeds.”
mil3.2.6:3.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to steal rice from another man …
mil3.2.6:3.4: Suppose, Great King, a certain man in the winter season were to light a fire, stir it up, and go away without putting it out, and that fire were to burn another man’s field, and the owner of the field, having seized him, were to show him to the king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, this man has burned my field’.
mil3.2.6:3.5: He would say: ‘Your Majesty, I did not burn this man’s field. The fire that I did not put out was one fire; the fire by which this man’s field was burned was another fire. I am not liable to punishment’.
mil3.2.6:3.6: Would that man be liable to punishment, Great King?”
mil3.2.6:3.9: “Even if he said so, venerable sir, since he cannot disown the earlier fire, that man would be liable to punishment because of the later fire.”
mil3.2.6:3.10: “In the same way, Great King, with this name and form one does a deed, good or bad, and by that deed another name and form is reborn; therefore he is not free from bad deeds.”
mil3.2.6:4.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to take a lamp, go up into a mansion, and eat his meal; the burning lamp were to set the straw alight, the burning straw were to set the house alight, and the burning house were to set the village alight; and the villagers, having seized that man, were to say: ‘Why, good man, did you set the village on fire?’ He would say: ‘Good sirs, I did not set the village on fire. The lamp-flame by whose light I ate was one fire; the fire by which the village was burned was another fire’. If they came into your presence disputing, whose case would you uphold, Great King?”
mil3.2.6:4.5: “Even if he said so, still that fire arose from that very flame.”
mil3.2.6:4.6: “In the same way, Great King, even though the name and form at the end of life is one, and the name and form at rebirth is another, still the latter arose from that very one; therefore he is not free from bad deeds.”
mil3.2.6:5.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to betroth a young girl, pay the bride-price, and go away.
mil3.2.6:5.3: After some time she would grow up, having come of age; then another man would pay the bride-price and marry her; and the first would come and say: ‘Why, good man, do you take my wife?’
mil3.2.6:5.4: He would say: ‘I am not taking your wife. The girl whom you betrothed and for whom you paid the bride-price was a young girl, a tender one; but this is another girl, grown up and come of age, whom I betrothed and for whom I paid the bride-price’. If they came into your presence disputing,
mil3.2.6:5.5: whose case would you uphold, Great King?”
mil3.2.6:5.8: “Even if he said so, still that grown girl came to be from that very girl.”
mil3.2.6:5.9: “In the same way, Great King, even though the name and form at the end of life is one, and the name and form at rebirth is another, still the latter arose from that very one; therefore he is not wholly free from bad deeds.”
mil3.2.6:6.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to buy a pot of milk from a cowherd’s hand, leave it in that very hand, and go away, thinking: ‘I will take it tomorrow’; and overnight it would turn into curd.
mil3.2.6:6.3: He would come back and say: ‘Give me my pot of milk’.
mil3.2.6:6.5: The other would say: ‘I did not buy curd from your hand; give me my pot of milk’.
mil3.2.6:6.6: He would say: ‘Without your knowing, your milk has turned into curd’. If they came into your presence disputing, whose case would you uphold, Great King?”
mil3.2.6:6.9: “Even if he said so, still it came to be from that very thing.”
mil3.2.6:6.10: “In the same way, Great King, even though the name and form at the end of life is one, and the name and form at rebirth is another, still the latter arose from that very one; therefore he is not wholly free from bad deeds.”
